## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

### Bug fixes

Isolated agents can now find and run the Action’s own `opencode` binary, fixing skills and scripts that check the host with `opencode --version`. It is appended after the runner’s existing PATH entries, so an earlier-installed `opencode` keeps precedence; the change also avoids duplicate entries and skips unknown paths. [#2251](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2251)

Subagent run logs now show each observed notice’s tag and metadata states, its classification, and whether background work is still running, followed by a per-child summary when the stream ends. This makes it easier to diagnose runs where subagent state appears inconsistent, without logging report bodies or descriptions; settlement and completion behavior remain unchanged. [#2254](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2254)


<details><summary>Full changelog</summary>

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

When an isolated agent needs to keep run records and hand-off data in the checkout, the Action can now accept an `agent-state-home` directory and temporarily hand it over as `XDG_STATE_HOME`. The path must be absolute, inside the checkout, and validated without following links; the input is ignored when isolation is off.

Repos cloned beneath the checkout are also trusted for the agent's Git operations, with a one-time warning and continued execution on Git versions older than 2.45.3. Nested state roots are handled as one take-back, and teardown restores runner ownership; if the runner cannot safely access the state, the take-back fails closed and leaves it alone. [#2245](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2245)


<details><summary>Full changelog</summary>

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

The Action no longer writes its GitHub token or config directory to `$GITHUB_ENV`, so later workflow steps do not inherit the Action's write token. The temporary `gh` config, which contains the token, is cleaned up after its last consumer, including in the post step if the main step was interrupted; cleanup refuses unsafe paths and symlinks. A later step that needs authenticated `gh` access must now provide its own `GH_TOKEN`. [#2242](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2242)

Repository skills now load independently under the existing staging limits: an oversized skill is skipped with a warning rather than preventing smaller skills from loading. Repositories named `.github` are also accepted, while invalid owner/repository paths remain refused. [#2244](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2244) [#2240](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2240)

When `gh auth login` exits before consuming its token input, setup now handles the resulting stdin error through the normal warning path instead of crashing with an unhandled `EPIPE`; login also has a 30-second timeout. The token remains on stdin rather than appearing in arguments or logs. [#2236](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2236)

Fro Bot can now publish a verdict on a pull request it authored by using a `COMMENT` review, since GitHub rejects approving or requesting changes on its own PR. The reviewed head and review body are preserved; fork PRs are still not approved, and an unknown bot login still fails closed. [#2241](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2241)


<details><summary>Full changelog</summary>

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Hosted workflows using `isolate-agent` can now share installed Playwright browsers, uv-managed Python versions, and mise tools with the isolated agent. The action gives the agent a private, writable runtime directory and passes through those tool-location settings only when the agent can access the directories; inaccessible locations are dropped and logged.

The setup and troubleshooting wiki now explains how to configure shared tool installs and documents related isolation behavior, including private XDG roots and provider-key proxy limits. [#2232](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2232) [#2231](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2231)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Published `fro-bot/agent` installs could be rejected by `isolate-agent` when invoked through a repository’s composite action, because the runner points `GITHUB_ACTION_PATH` at the wrapper rather than the installed action. Preflight now identifies the install from the running `dist/main.js` bundle and validates the corresponding `_actions` path against the runner-provided repository and ref.

Local `uses: ./` installs remain refused, and the action’s main and post stages continue to resolve to the same reference-derived installation. [#2225](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2225)
